Analyzing openmasterhub-bin AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD contains only standard, static variable declarations at the global (top-level) scope. Every line that would execute during `makepkg --printsrcinfo` — the variable assignments for `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `optdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `install`, `source`, and `sha256sums` — consists solely of literal strings and array literals. There are no command substitutions, no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget`, no network operations, and no encoded or obfuscated payloads.

The `source` entry references a GitHub releases URL for the package's own binary tarball (`github.com/hoxton314/openmasterhub`), but this URL is never fetched or parsed during `--printsrcinfo` — sourcing a PKGBUILD only reads the array definition, it does not download anything. No unrelated or untrusted host is contacted. The `install=openmasterhub.install` reference points to a local install file in the same package; referencing it is metadata only and does not source or execute it.

The `package()` function contains only ordinary `install -Dm755`/`install -Dm644` copying of the package's own files into `$pkgdir`, plus a udev rules file and a systemd user service — all standard packaging for this application. It is out of scope for this gate anyway, as function bodies are never executed during `--printsrcinfo`. The `sha256sums` value is a genuine checksum (not `SKIP`), and per the audit rules a `SKIP` value would also not be grounds for failure at this step. No malicious behavior is present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Top-level scope is clean; only static declarations and a local install reference present
</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This .SRCINFO file is a clean, standard AUR manifest for a prebuilt binary package (`openmasterhub-bin`, the `-bin` variant of `openmasterhub`). It declares dependencies on expected GNOME/GTK desktop libraries (webkit2gtk-4.1, gtk3, glibc, gcc-libs, systemd), lists reasonable optional dependencies, and references the package's own upstream GitHub repository at https://github.com/hoxton314/openmasterhub.

The only network action is fetching the package's own precompiled tarball from the project's official GitHub releases page (v0.3.0), which is exactly what a `-bin` package is meant to do. A valid, non-SKIP sha256sum is provided for integrity verification.

I found no obfuscation, no encoded or eval'd commands, no exfiltration attempts, no reverse shells, and no fetching of executable content from unrelated hosts. There is no install script or build logic embedded in this file to analyze — it is purely declarative metadata. This is ordinary, well-formed packaging practice with no evidence of a supply-chain attack.
</details>
